page.layout: One text column in the centre, with small marginal notes down the left side. Right of the text is the edge of the neighbouring page, which is not transcribed. Printed page 26 at top left, running head at top centre, catchword at the foot right.

main_text.p: teria & motu fenfibili paulo remotiores, & notiores sunt nobis quæ fensui (unde plurima noftra cognitio oritur) propinquiores ; tum etiam ob mutuam inter se connexionem cognationemque. At rem manifestam, & vulgò notam, quæ est in quotidiano usu & in omnium ore, cujúsque vim & motus nemo est qui non sentiat, definiendo non tam illustrasti, inquietis, quàm obscurâsti. Equidem nihil hinc aliud fidere possum : nimirum, sic sunt inanes nostræ hominum cogitationes omnes & universi conatus. Quæ sunt ante pedes & oculos, quæ in sensus & animos incurrunt, quæ sunt lippis & tonsoribus haud ignota, quæ capere se putant, & quidem suo modo capiunt illiteratissimi quique homunciones; hæc ipsa non capiunt Eccl. 7 [?]acutissimi Philosophi : In his vel subtilissimis ingeniis aqua hæret. Tempus, Locus, Motus, id genus plurima, quid sibi velint, & quid sint, quotusquisque est hominum nostrorum, qui non existimet se perfectissimè intelligere? in quorum naturâ indagandâ, eruendâ, explicandâ, Doctores profundi subtiles, Angelici, Seraphici, per multa retrò secula velut in palestrâ se exercuerunt, exercentque etiamnum, nec potuerunt hactenus post tantum sudoris & pulveris optatam metam contingere. In tempore sum, & de tempore loquor, & tamen nescio quid sit tempus, inquit, Augustinus initio libri de Tempore. Quâ in re nequeo satis admirari Dei Opt. Max. infinitam sapientiam, retundentis hoc pacto humanam superbiam, & repræsentantis mortalibus velut in speculo inanem illam ἀδυναμοφίαν [?] quâ sibi videtur aliquid esse, cum nihil sint, miserè decipientes cor suum.Gal. 6. 3. Ut scilicet discant homunciones Horat. [?]metiri se modulo ac pede suo, nec sapere ultrà quàm par est, sed sapere ad sobrietatem agnoscentes insipientiam suam, ut Deo integra constet sapientiæ suæ gloria.

page.notes: Left margin, top: a note of several lines, largely illegible at this scan, beginning "Odi ego" [illegible, ~20 letters]; transcribed only as far as legible. Margin references "Augustin. 2. de Ord. 2" and "Gal. 6. 3." read with doubt. Footnote numbers 1, 2, 3 in the text correspond to the small notes at the left margin; their exact wording is doubtful and marked [?]. The Greek word ἀδυναμοφίαν is uncertain in its letters. Some marginal notes near the top left are too faint to read and are not transcribed. The signature at foot right, "P R Æ", is taken as the catchword and is uncertain.
